## 3. The Integration Question

```{r}
#| label: join-safety
#| include: false
# Join-safety proof: the weather extract must be one row per date, or the
# join manufactures trips. The warehouse's PRIMARY KEY guarantees it; verify
# anyway, in the open, and show the row count is unchanged by the join.
wx_rows  <- nrow(weather)
wx_dates <- n_distinct(weather$date)
stopifnot(wx_rows == wx_dates)
```

<!-- TODO: this is the project's centerpiece and it is yours.
     Build the two-year daily table (comparable window, both years), join the
     audited weather with the row-count proof, handle the sentinel days with
     a visible count, fit the naive comparison AND the weather-adjusted
     model, report the year effect with its interval, interpret it honestly
     (what does the year term bundle?), and produce the figure. -->
```{r}
#| label: integration-question

# Keep the same January 1–October 11 window for both years (comparable window).
integration_trips <- daily |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(
    (date >= as.Date("2025-01-01") &
       date <= as.Date("2025-10-11")) |
    (date >= as.Date("2026-01-01") &
       date <= as.Date("2026-10-11"))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(lubridate::year(date)),
    non_member = casual + day_pass,
    weekday = factor(lubridate::wday(date, label = TRUE)),
    month = factor(lubridate::month(date, label = TRUE))
  )

# Record the trip-row count before joining weather.
trip_rows_before <- nrow(integration_trips)

# Mark weather records so unmatched dates can be distinguished
# from dates with missing precipitations.
weather_join <- weather |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    weather_match = TRUE
  )

# Join weather to the daily trip records.
integration_daily <- integration_trips |>
  left_join(weather_join, by = "date")

# Verify that the join did not create or remove trip rows.
trip_rows_after <- nrow(integration_daily)

stopifnot(trip_rows_before == trip_rows_after)
stopifnot(n_distinct(integration_daily$date) == trip_rows_after)

# Count unmatched weather dates (should not affect b/c these dates are not in our comparison window
unmatched_weather <- sum(is.na(integration_daily$weather_match))

# Count missing precipitation values (reported as NA in tibble)
sentinel_precip_days <- sum(
  !is.na(integration_daily$weather_match) &
    is.na(integration_daily$precip_in)
)

# Display the audit results as a tibble.
integration_audit <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "Daily trip records before weather join",
    "Daily trip records after weather join",
    "Unique daily dates after join",
    "2025 daily records",
    "2026 daily records",
    "Dates without a matching weather record",
    "Matched dates with missing precipitation"
  ),
  Result = c(
    trip_rows_before,
    trip_rows_after,
    n_distinct(integration_daily$date),
    sum(integration_daily$year == "2025"),
    sum(integration_daily$year == "2026"),
    unmatched_weather,
    sentinel_precip_days
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  integration_audit,
  col.names = c("Integration audit check", "Result"),
  caption = "Daily trip and weather integration audit"
)
```

The weather join preserved all `568` daily trip records, confirming that the join did not change the number of observations. The comparison includes `284` days from each year, covering the same January 1–October 11 dates chosen as the acceptable comparison window. All trip dates had a corresponding weather record. However, precipitation was missing for `6` matched dates because sentinel values had been converted to missing values during warehouse loading. These observations will be excluded from analyses requiring precipitation rather than treating missing values as zero. Lastly, in the following analyses, day pass riders are counted as non-members to ensure there are two categories (members and non-members (casual and day pass riders)).

```{r}
#| label: modeling-sample-audit

# Count usable observations for each model, separately by year.
model_sample_audit <- integration_daily |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    naive_model_days = n(),
    adjusted_model_days = sum(
      complete.cases(tmax_f, tmin_f, precip_in)
    ),
    excluded_from_adjusted = naive_model_days - adjusted_model_days,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  model_sample_audit,
  col.names = c(
    "Year",
    "Naive model days",
    "Weather-adjusted model days",
    "Days excluded from adjusted model"
  ),
  caption = "Available observations for each model"
)

# Show dates with missing precipitation.
missing_precip_dates <- integration_daily |>
  filter(is.na(precip_in)) |>
  select(date, year, tmax_f, tmin_f, precip_in)

knitr::kable(
  missing_precip_dates,
  caption = "Dates with missing precipitation values"
)

# Complete data for the weather-adjusted model.
weather_model_data <- integration_daily |>
  filter(complete.cases(tmax_f, tmin_f, precip_in))
```

```{r}
#| label: integration-models

# Naive model: compares average daily non-member trips by year.
# Uses all 568 daily observations (includes dates with missing precipitation values).
naive_model <- lm(
  non_member ~ year,
  data = integration_daily
)

# Weather-adjusted model: adds weather and calendar controls.
# Uses only observations with complete weather data.
adjusted_model <- lm(
  non_member ~ year + tmax_f + tmin_f + precip_in + weekday + month,
  data = weather_model_data
)

# Extract the year effect and its 95% confidence interval.
naive_year_effect <- broom::tidy(
  naive_model,
  conf.int = TRUE
) |>
  filter(term == "year2026") |>
  mutate(model = "Naive")

adjusted_year_effect <- broom::tidy(
  adjusted_model,
  conf.int = TRUE
) |>
  filter(term == "year2026") |>
  mutate(model = "Weather-adjusted")

# Combine the year effects into one comparison table.
year_effects <- bind_rows(
  naive_year_effect,
  adjusted_year_effect
) |>
  select(
    model,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  )

knitr::kable(
  year_effects,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Model",
    "2026 year effect (trips/day)",
    "95% CI lower",
    "95% CI upper",
    "p-value"
  ),
  caption = "Comparison of the 2026 year effect before and after weather/calendar adjustment"
)
```


```{r}
#| label: integration-figure
#| fig-cap: "Daily non-member trips during the comparable January 1–October 11 periods in 2025 and 2026. Lines show separate linear trends for each year."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

integration_plot <- ggplot(
  integration_daily,
  aes(x = date, y = non_member, color = year)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusting for weather, 2026 ran 40.48 more non-member trips per day than 2025, 95% CI [30.96, 50.00]", # Otherwise, 2026 ran 30.69 more non-member trips per day than 2025, 95% CI [9.77, 51.62]
    subtitle = "Comparable January 1–October 11 periods between 2025 and 2026",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Daily non-member trips",
    color = "Year",
    caption = "n = 562 trips/year, Ride Knox export."
  ) +
  theme_board

integration_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "figs/integration_daily_trips.png",
  plot = integration_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

### Interpretation
For the model analyses, 2025 includes casual riders only as non-member riders, while 2026 bundles casual and day pass riders as non-member riders. The naive model estimates that 2026 averaged 30.69 more non-member trips per day than 2025 (95% CI [9.77–51.62]). After adjusting for maximum temperature, minimum temperature, precipitation, weekday, and month, the estimated average difference increased to 40.48 more non-member trips per day between  2025 and 2026 (95% CI [30.96–50.00]; see figs/integration_daily_trips.png). The larger adjusted estimate/model suggests that weather and calendar structures account for **some** variation in daily non-member trips across years, information not available in the naive model. However, these adjustments do not establish the cause of that increase from the naive model.
